title: 1988 AHSME Problem 27
statement: In the figure, \(AB\perp BC,\) \(BC\perp CD,\) and \(BC\) is tangent to the circle with center \(O\) and diameter \(AD.\) In which one of the following cases is the area of \(ABCD\) an integer?

solutions.text:
The tangent point is the midpoint of \(BC,\) and the tangent-secant relation gives \((\frac{BC}{2})^2=AB\cdot CD.\) Thus \(BC=2\sqrt{AB\cdot CD},\) and the trapezoid area is \[ \begin{aligned} \text{Area} &=\frac{AB+CD}{2}BC\\ &=(AB+CD)\sqrt{AB\cdot CD}. \end{aligned} \] Only \(AB=9,\ CD=4\) makes the product under the radical a square; the area is \(13\cdot6=78.\)

Thus the correct answer is D.
hints: Let the tangent point be \(M\) and use the diameter to form a rectangle inside the trapezoid
Power of point \(B\) relates half of \(BC\) to \(AB\) and \(CD\)
